hunks.baseline: From the moment good and evil first split apart, things that would never disappear from the world were born.
hunks.sol: From the moment good and evil first parted ways, certain things had existed in the world that would never disappear.

hunks.baseline: Those called bandits were among them.
hunks.sol: Bandits were among them.

hunks.baseline: They robbed and stole wealth, and sometimes even took other people’s lives in the process. They had existed since time immemorial and were the kind of people who could never be rooted out completely.
hunks.sol: They stole and plundered, sometimes taking lives in the process. They had been around since time immemorial, and no one had ever managed to root them out.

hunks.baseline: Just as shadows fell wherever there was light, the wheel could not be stopped unless people were rid of the desires and emotions everyone felt.
hunks.sol: Where there was light, there would be shadows. As long as people felt desire and emotion, that wheel would keep turning.

hunks.baseline: Perhaps that was why people had finally decided to accept this unpleasant natural order.
Rather than spill innocent blood trying to break an unbreakable cycle, they had come to tolerate a certain degree of coexistence through talking things out.
hunks.sol: Perhaps that was why people had finally accepted this unpleasant fact of life. Rather than spill innocent blood trying to break an unbreakable cycle, they had come to tolerate a measure of coexistence through negotiation.

hunks.baseline: But people could sense that the long stretch of coexistence was now rushing toward its end.
hunks.sol: But now they could sense that the long years of coexistence were coming to an end.

hunks.baseline: The people of county towns near mountains and rivers felt the unusual atmosphere keenly.
hunks.sol: In the county towns near the mountains and rivers, people could feel that something was wrong.

hunks.baseline: “What do you mean, it wasn’t an ordinary landslide?”
hunks.sol: “What do you mean, not an ordinary landslide?”

hunks.baseline: “I’ve spent my whole fifty years plowing fields, so I can’t say for sure. But those folks can tell at a glance.”
hunks.sol: “I’ve spent all fifty years of my life plowing fields, so I can’t say for sure. But those fellows know what they’re looking at.”

hunks.baseline: “The herb gatherers took one look at the cut ends of the trees swept down with the earth and sand. They hadn’t been bent and snapped clean off—it looked as though someone had given them a few halfhearted chops with an axe. Besides, there weren’t any real signs of a landslide to begin with.”
hunks.sol: “They looked at the ends of the trees swept down with the earth and sand. The trunks hadn’t just bent and snapped. It looked as if someone had taken a few halfhearted swings at them with an axe. And there’d been no real sign of a landslide beforehand.”

hunks.baseline: “Shh! ‘Those damn bandits’? Watch your mouth. It’s unlikely, but if the Green Forest Alliance hears you…”
hunks.sol: “Shh! ‘Those damn bandits’? Watch your mouth. It’s unlikely, but if someone from the Green Forest Alliance hears you…”

hunks.baseline: “Green Forest Alliance, my ass. What’s wrong with calling bandits bandits? They’re highwaymen who take two days’ wages just to let you cross a mountain pass!”
hunks.sol: “Green Forest Alliance, my ass. What’s wrong with calling bandits bandits? Those highwaymen take two days’ wages just to let you cross a mountain pass!”

hunks.baseline: “That man’s right. Everyone knows bandits are no good, but they’re not completely out of control like Dark Heaven. Something like this happened when we were kids, too, didn’t it?”
hunks.sol: “He’s right. Everyone knows bandits are no good, but they’re not like Dark Heaven, running completely wild. Something similar happened when we were kids, didn’t it?”

hunks.baseline: “Right. Though it wasn’t Dark Heaven back then, it was the Demonic Cult. Anyway, I remember the Green Forest Alliance joining forces with the Murim Alliance to fight them. The Green Forest Alliance was formed afterward.”
hunks.sol: “Right. It was the Demonic Cult back then, not Dark Heaven. But I remember the bandits joining forces with the Murim Alliance to fight them. The Green Forest Alliance was formed afterward.”

hunks.baseline: For middle-aged men who were getting on in years, the Great Faction War was one of those childhood memories they would never forget.
hunks.sol: To these middle-aged men, now well along in years, the Great Faction War was an unforgettable childhood memory.

hunks.baseline: Ordinary people had suffered little harm, but the news that bloodthirsty murderers who believed in an evil doctrine had invaded the Central Plains had thrown the whole land into turmoil.
hunks.sol: Ordinary people had suffered little harm, but news that murderers devoted to an evil doctrine had invaded the Central Plains had thrown the whole land into turmoil.

hunks.baseline: So even with these ominous rumors about the Green Forest Alliance, people couldn’t help but remain skeptical. The Green Forest Alliance they remembered was a group formed by bandits who were at least willing to talk. They had long since become a part of everyday life.
hunks.sol: So even amid the troubling rumors about the Green Forest Alliance, people couldn’t quite believe them. The alliance they remembered had been formed by bandits who could at least be reasoned with. It had long since become a part of everyday life.

hunks.baseline: But that wasn’t the only rumor going around.
hunks.sol: But there were other rumors, too.

hunks.baseline: “Do you remember those men who passed through our village in the dead of night two days ago?”
hunks.sol: “Remember those men who passed through our village in the dead of night two days ago?”

hunks.baseline: “Of course. You mean those strangers? I think they called themselves the Blue Flower Escort Bureau.”
hunks.sol: “Of course. You mean those strangers? I think they said they were from the Blue Flower Escort Bureau.”

hunks.baseline: “Right, those men. I was shocked to see one of their porters, big as an ox, holding up that heavy flag without even blinking. Then I got a second shock when I saw his face—it was even more terrifying than his build.”
hunks.sol: “Right, those men. One of their caravan porters was big as an ox, and he held up that heavy flag without batting an eye. That startled me enough, but then I saw his face. He looked even fiercer than he was big.”

hunks.baseline: “Why bring that up now? Merchants and escort bureaus pass through here several times a month. It’s nothing unusual.”
hunks.sol: “Why bring them up now? Merchants and escort bureaus pass through here several times a month. There’s nothing unusual about that.”

hunks.baseline: At the others’ puzzled looks, the middle-aged man who’d started the conversation lowered his voice.
hunks.sol: At the others’ puzzled looks, the middle-aged man who had brought it up lowered his voice.

hunks.baseline: “They did come through, but where they went in the end—that’s what matters, isn’t it?”
hunks.sol: “They came through, yes. But what matters is where they ended up.”

hunks.baseline: The next moment, the middle-aged man pulled a bundled piece of cloth from his robe and unfolded it. Everyone who saw it widened their eyes.
hunks.sol: He took a bundle of cloth from inside his robe and unfolded it. The others’ eyes widened as dried earth and grains of sand fell away, revealing two characters.

hunks.baseline: More precisely, they stared at the two characters revealed as the dried mud and grains of sand fell away.
“If you remember that big porter, you’ll remember the flag he was carrying, too. That’s right. It’s their escort flag.”
hunks.sol: “If you remember that big porter, you’ll remember the flag he was carrying. That’s right. This is the escort bureau’s flag.”

hunks.baseline: The villagers looked at one another and swallowed hard.
hunks.sol: They looked at one another and swallowed hard.

hunks.baseline: A flag held great symbolic meaning for any group.
Just as soldiers would give their lives to protect a general’s banner, the merchants and escort bureaus they knew took pride in their own flags.
hunks.sol: A flag meant something to any group. Soldiers would give their lives to protect their commander’s banner, and the merchants and escort bureaus these people knew took pride in their flags, too.

hunks.baseline: But what if an escort bureau’s flag, carried along the mountain road in the dead of night just two days ago, had turned up in the landslide?
hunks.sol: So what did it mean that the flag of an escort bureau that had taken the mountain road just two nights ago had turned up buried in a landslide? That a suspicious landslide had blocked the only way through barely a day later?

hunks.baseline: And what if a suspicious landslide had blocked the only road through the mountains a day later?

“I’m not guessing. That’s exactly what happened. The Green Forest Alliance—those damned bandits—must have pulled something. For some reason, they killed to silence whoever knew, then tried to cover it up by passing it off as a landslide.”
hunks.sol: “It’s not a question of what I think. The Green Forest Alliance—those damned bandits—must have done something. For some reason, they killed to silence the witnesses, then tried to hide it with a staged landslide.”

hunks.baseline: A suffocating silence pressed down on the group.
hunks.sol: A suffocating silence settled over them.

hunks.baseline: Their unease, now unmistakably real, tightened like a noose around their necks as the pieces of the situation fell neatly into place.
hunks.sol: Their fears were taking shape, and every detail seemed to fit. The thought left them struggling to breathe.

hunks.baseline: “B-But what would they have to gain from doing that? They fought the Demonic Cult in the past. As a reward, they got to call themselves an alliance, like the river pirates on the Yangtze, and live pretty comfortably.”
hunks.sol: “B-But what would they have to gain? They fought the Demonic Cult in the past. As a reward, they got to call themselves an alliance, like the river pirates on the Yangtze, and live well enough.”

hunks.baseline: “Do you remember what you said during the harvest two years ago?”
hunks.sol: “Remember what you said at the harvest two years ago?”

hunks.baseline: “You were disappointed. It was the best harvest in nearly ten years, but you sighed and said it still wasn’t enough. Would those men be any different?”
hunks.sol: “You were disappointed. It was the best harvest in nearly ten years, but you sighed and said it still wasn’t enough. Why would those men be any different?”

hunks.baseline: “It’s obvious. Even we farmers get greedy. What about men who make their living taking what belongs to others?”
hunks.sol: “Even we farmers get greedy. Imagine men who make their living taking what belongs to others.”

hunks.baseline: Even if their paths were different, some things still fit.
hunks.sol: Their circumstances were different, but the comparison held.

hunks.baseline: The middle-aged tenant farmer was only speaking from what he’d learned himself and his prejudice against bandits. But his argument made plenty of sense.
hunks.sol: The middle-aged tenant farmer was speaking only from his own experience and his low opinion of bandits. Still, there was reason enough behind what he said.

hunks.baseline: Anyone who won this gamble could become a true king of a nation, instead of merely being called one of the Ten Kings.
hunks.sol: Anyone who won that gamble might become a king of a nation in truth, rather than merely bear a title among the Ten Kings.

hunks.baseline: Among all the news that had reached this little village, there was also a story far more shocking than the still-unconfirmed rumors of the Green Forest Alliance’s betrayal.
hunks.sol: And among the news that had reached this little village was a story far more shocking than the still-unconfirmed rumors of the Green Forest Alliance’s betrayal.

hunks.baseline: “Even the Murong Family of the orthodox faction—the one supposedly full of Great Heroes of Benevolence and Righteousness—joined forces with those vicious enemies. What do you expect from a bunch of thieves?”
hunks.sol: “Even the Murong Family of the orthodox faction—the one supposedly full of Great Heroes of Benevolence and Righteousness—joined forces with those vicious enemies. Why wouldn’t a bunch of thieves?”

hunks.baseline: At the mention of the Murong Family, one of the Five Great Families, which had unleashed a bloodbath across the northern lands, the others shut their mouths as if on cue.
hunks.sol: At the mention of the Murong Family, one of the Five Great Families, said to have unleashed a bloodbath across the northern lands, the others fell silent as if on cue.

hunks.baseline: That was right.
For people born bandits, whose whole purpose in life was to take what they wanted, why would betrayal matter?
hunks.sol: Of course. Those men were bandits by nature. Taking from others was their way of life. Why would betrayal trouble them?

hunks.baseline: If they could win this enormous gamble and survive to the end, they would gain wealth and glory beyond anything they’d known before.
hunks.sol: If they won this enormous gamble—if they survived to the end—they could gain wealth and glory beyond anything they had known before.

hunks.baseline: “What a turbulent age we live in.”
hunks.sol: “What an age of chaos.”

hunks.baseline: The old man’s quiet murmur from his place in the corner spoke for everyone. Then his next words, breathed out like a sigh, fanned the unease already boiling inside them.
hunks.sol: The old man sitting in the corner had quietly voiced what they were all thinking. His next words came out like a sigh and fed their mounting unease.

hunks.baseline: “With the mountains in such an uproar, the rivers will be in turmoil, too.”
hunks.sol: “With the mountains in such an uproar, the river won’t stay calm.”

hunks.baseline: And soon enough, his words became reality.
hunks.sol: Soon, his words came true.

hunks.baseline: If you asked whose the vast, boundless Yangtze was, those in the Murim would answer without hesitation.
hunks.sol: Ask anyone in Murim who owned the vast Yangtze, and they would answer without hesitation.

hunks.baseline: Not one of the Five Great Families or the Nine Sects and One Gang—but the Yangtze River Channel League.
hunks.sol: Not the Five Great Families or the Nine Sects and One Gang. The Yangtze River Channel League.

hunks.baseline: But those outside the Murim would give a different answer.
hunks.sol: But those outside Murim would give a different answer. Mountain or river, everything beneath the lofty sky had only one master.

hunks.baseline: To them, whether you were talking about mountains or rivers, there was only one master of all things beneath the lofty sky.
And the Seafaring King, Pa Ryun, had never liked that one bit.
hunks.sol: Seafaring King Pa Ryun had never liked that one bit.

hunks.baseline: “When this old man was a child, an old man who lived next door told me that the Son of Heaven was descended from dragons, a child of Heaven who must be served with all one’s heart and soul.”
hunks.sol: “When this old man was a child, an old man who lived next door told me the Son of Heaven had dragon blood in his veins. A child of Heaven, he said, who must be served with all one’s heart and soul.”

hunks.baseline: His voice was low, but full of force. His profound internal energy made the air tremble.
hunks.sol: His voice was low but carried force, and his profound internal energy made the space around him tremble.

hunks.baseline: “He had a bad temper, but he was a decent enough old man. When I was orphaned by one bad harvest after another, he took me in for a while.”
hunks.sol: “He had a foul temper, but he was decent enough. After one famine after another took my parents, he took me in for a while.”

hunks.baseline: Pa Ryun looked back on his past, lost in thought.
hunks.sol: Pa Ryun’s gaze grew distant as he looked back on his past.

hunks.baseline: He had gone over it hundreds, thousands of times already, but it was full of nothing but bad memories.

hunks.baseline: He had lost both parents before he could grow a beard, and the time he spent in harsh servitude under the old man, just managing to keep food in his mouth, had been the best part of his life.
hunks.sol: He had gone over those memories hundreds, thousands of times. Almost none were good. He had lost both parents before he was old enough to grow a beard, and being taken in by that old man—working hard as a servant just to get enough to eat—had been among the better times.

hunks.baseline: Of course, even that didn’t last long.
hunks.sol: Even that hadn’t lasted.

hunks.baseline: “It was a damnable time. More than ten fools called themselves kings, and the so-called imperial troops could raid villages in broad daylight, looting and killing, without facing any consequences.”
hunks.sol: “It was a damnable age. More than ten fools called themselves kings, and so-called imperial troops could march into a village in broad daylight, loot it, and kill its people without anyone holding them to account.”

hunks.baseline: It was the same old story.
The old man had died then.
hunks.sol: It was a familiar story. The old man had died then.

hunks.baseline: Not at the hands of a defeated army or bandits, but the imperial troops marching forward with sharp spears and tall banners.
hunks.sol: Not at the hands of routed soldiers or bandits, but at the hands of imperial troops marching under tall banners with sharpened spears and swords.

hunks.baseline: The twelve-year-old boy, grateful to the old man, killed the soldier who had driven a spear into the old man’s frail body, then ran.
hunks.sol: The twelve-year-old boy, grateful to the old man, had killed the soldier who drove a spear into his frail body. Then he ran.

hunks.baseline: “I ran for three days and nights without stopping. In the end, I escaped their pursuit, reached a riverbank, and collapsed. Then a thought came to me.”
hunks.sol: “I ran for three days and nights without stopping. I finally shook off my pursuers, reached the riverbank, and collapsed. And a thought came to me.”

hunks.baseline: Pa Ryun pointed to the sky as he continued.
hunks.sol: Pa Ryun pointed at the sky.

hunks.baseline: “There were so many people claiming the world belonged to them. If the so-called children of Heaven were like that, who was I supposed to serve?”
hunks.sol: “So many men claimed the world was theirs. If those who called themselves children of Heaven behaved like that, who was I supposed to serve?”

hunks.baseline: In the end, the long age of chaos came to an end.
hunks.sol: The long age of chaos eventually ended.

hunks.baseline: A hero of the Zhu family unified the continent and announced to all under Heaven that he alone was the Son of Heaven.
hunks.sol: A hero surnamed Zhu unified the continent and proclaimed to all under Heaven that he alone was the Son of Heaven.

hunks.baseline: By then, the boy had become a young man, and Pa Ryun had become a river pirate instead of a servant. Watching the new Son of Heaven ascend the throne, he found the answer to his question.
hunks.sol: By then, the boy had become a young man, and the servant had become a river pirate. Watching the new Son of Heaven ascend the throne, Pa Ryun found his answer.

hunks.baseline: “That was when I learned that anything could be won with spears and swords. That only the last one standing could prove himself by the outcome.”
hunks.sol: “That was when I learned that anything could be won with spears and swords. Only the final victor could prove his claim through the outcome.”

hunks.baseline: But Pa Ryun knew his own limits better than anyone.

hunks.baseline: He had neither the right to claim the world nor the strength to take it.
hunks.sol: But Pa Ryun knew his own limits better than anyone. He had neither a cause that would let him claim the world nor the strength to take it.

hunks.baseline: Still, he had been able to claim this great river.
hunks.sol: He could, however, take this vast river.

hunks.baseline: And with it, hundreds of ships and thousands of men—enough to stand against the Great Nation’s warships, now visible in the distance.
hunks.sol: And with it came hundreds of ships and thousands of men—enough to face the Great Nation’s warships now appearing in the distance.

hunks.baseline: *Whoosh.*
hunks.sol: *Fwoosh.*

hunks.baseline: Above Pa Ryun’s bright smile, a great sheet of cloth snapped in the wind.
hunks.sol: A great expanse of cloth billowed above Pa Ryun’s broad smile.

hunks.baseline: As countless ships surged forward beneath it, the black-robed man at Pa Ryun’s side quietly curled his lips into a smile.
hunks.sol: As countless ships followed the flag, the black-clad man at his side quietly curled his lips into a smile.
